subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Relative masses of atoms and molecules
The mole and the Avogadro constant

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explain: Water consists of two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom, giving the formula H2O.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of carbon dioxide?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide contains one carbon atom bonded to two oxygen atoms, giving CO2.

questions.q: What does the empirical formula of a compound show?
options: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element present
The actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule
The total mass of the compound
The number of moles in one gram of the compound
questions.explain: The empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.

questions.q: What does the molecular formula of a compound show?
options: The actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule
The simplest ratio of atoms present
The percentage of each element by mass
The relative atomic mass of each element
questions.explain: The molecular formula shows the actual numbers of atoms of each element in one molecule of the compound.

questions.q: Magnesium ions are Mg2+ and chloride ions are Cl-. What is the formula of magnesium chloride?
questions.explain: Two Cl- ions are needed to balance one Mg2+ ion, giving the neutral formula MgCl2.

questions.q: The ammonium ion is NH4+ and the sulfate ion is SO4^2-. What is the formula of ammonium sulfate?
questions.explain: Two NH4+ ions balance one SO4^2- ion, so the formula is (NH4)2SO4 with brackets around the ammonium group.

questions.q: Glucose has the molecular formula C6H12O6. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: Dividing the subscripts 6:12:6 by their common factor of 6 gives the simplest ratio CH2O.

questions.q: The relative atomic mass (Ar) of an element is measured relative to which standard?
questions.explain: Relative atomic masses are measured on a scale where an atom of carbon-12 has a mass of exactly 12 units.

questions.q: Why is the relative atomic mass of chlorine given as 35.5 rather than a whole number?
options: It is an average that accounts for the different isotopes of chlorine
Chlorine atoms lose half an electron
It includes the mass of the electrons
The value has been rounded incorrectly
questions.explain: The Ar is a weighted average of the masses of chlorine's isotopes and their relative abundances, giving 35.5.

questions.q: Using Ar(H) = 1 and Ar(O) = 16, what is the relative molecular mass (Mr) of water, H2O?
Using Ar(C) = 12 and Ar(O) = 16, what is the Mr of carbon dioxide, CO2?
Using Ar values Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16, what is the Mr of calcium carbonate, CaCO3?
How is the relative molecular mass (Mr) of a compound calculated?
options: By adding together the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in the formula
By multiplying the relative atomic masses of all the atoms
By dividing the mass by the number of moles
By counting the number of atoms in the molecule
questions.explain: The Mr is found by adding up the Ar values of every atom shown in the compound's formula.

questions.q: What is the approximate value of the Avogadro constant?
questions.explain: The Avogadro constant is 6.02 x 10^23, the number of particles in one mole of a substance.

questions.q: What is a mole of a substance defined as?
options: The amount containing the same number of particles as the Avogadro constant
The mass of one atom of the substance
The volume of one gram of the substance
The number of protons in an atom
questions.explain: One mole is the amount of substance that contains 6.02 x 10^23 particles, equal to the Avogadro constant.

questions.q: Which equation correctly links the number of moles, mass and relative formula mass?
questions.explain: The number of moles is found by dividing the mass in grams by the relative formula mass (Mr).

questions.q: How many moles are there in 36 g of water (Mr of H2O = 18)?
questions.explain: moles = mass / Mr = 36 / 18 = 2 moles.

questions.q: What is the mass of 0.5 moles of carbon dioxide (Mr of CO2 = 44)?
questions.explain: mass = moles x Mr = 0.5 x 44 = 22 g.

questions.q: How many molecules are there in 2 moles of a gas (Avogadro constant = 6.02 x 10^23)?
questions.explain: Number of molecules = 2 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 1.204 x 10^24.

questions.q: How many atoms of oxygen are present in one mole of carbon dioxide, CO2?
questions.explain: Each CO2 molecule has 2 oxygen atoms, so one mole contains 2 x 6.02 x 10^23 = 1.204 x 10^24 oxygen atoms.
